newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended lower in quiet trade. News that Turkey will not have to import sugar in 1997 was nothing new and had no impact on prices. October closed $0.30 higher at $348.00. In New York raw sugar futures settled a thinly-traded session barely moved from opening levels, as prices tended to be more stable after a volatile week. October climbed to an 18-months high of 12.20 cents/lb earlier this week on mostly fund buying which, however, was not supported by fundamentals.

There is a large open speculative long position in October, which could put the October contract under pressure and narrow the October/March spread of 31 points with some traders forecasting the spread to fall to under 20 points. The row between the Ukraine and Russia over import taxes is going on. Ukrainian president Leonid Kuchma recently said that Russia's proposal to tax Ukrainian imports could spark a trade war and spoil much improved relations between the two most powerful former Soviet republics. The Russian government in August said it would slap a value-added tax of about 20 percent on Ukrainian imports to curb what Russian producers say is mass dumping of cut-price goods on their markets.

The measures, including a one million tonnes quota for sugar imports from CIS states, were postponed until October after crisis talks in Moscow between the two countries' Prime Ministers. Ukraine says the moves are discriminatory and violate a free trade agreement signed within the context of the 12-nation Commonwealth of Independent States. Most of Ukraine's 1.4 million tonnes of sugar exports in 1996 have gone to Russia, Ukrainian sources said.

IRELAND - The latest beet test results of September 6, 1996 show a very satisfactory increase in root weight while sugar content is still lagging behind the previous year's excellent results and the five-year average. Root weight amounted to 48.16 tonnes per ha, up from last year's 43.83 and the five-year average (1991/95) of 42.30 tonnes. Sugar content rose by 0.46 percentage points to 13.97 per cent, down from 16.59 percent in 1995 and the five-year average of 15.02 percent. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight of 6.72 tonnes, white value, per ha, down 7.3 percent on last year's 7.25 tonnes, but up 8 percent on the average of 6.22 tonnes. Even though last year's excellent results will be out of reach, the overall harvest will achieve very satisfactory results.

SWEDEN - The Swedish beet test results continue to be disappointing. Beet weight on September 2 amounted to no more than 38.0 tonnes, down from last year's 38.5 tonnes and sharply below the five-year average (1991/95) of 41.3 tonnes. Sugar content dropped to 15.7 per cent against 17.1 per cent in 1995 and 15.6 per cent in 1991/95. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight of 5.95 tonnes, white value, 9.7 per cent down on last year's 6.59 tonnes and 7.9 per cent below the five-year average. Despite these rather subdued tests, industry sources expect total production to be around 402,000 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 387,000 tonnes.

TAIWAN - Sugar production in March 1996 amounted to 91,650 tonnes, raw value, against 98,887 tonnes in March 1995. This brought cumulative production in the first five months of 1995/96 (November/March) up to 416,493 tonnes, marginally below last year's 417,642 tonnes. Total production in 1994/95 amounted to 443,470 tonnes compared to 509,201 tonnes in 1993/94.

FINLAND - Sugar exports in March 1996 reached 6,730 tonnes, raw value, which brought cumulative exports in the first half of 1995/96 (October/March) up to 31,781 tonnes compared to 4,239 in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 6,763 tonnes, down from 15,127 in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in Oct/Mar 1995/96 were Russia with 8,348 tonnes whites against 331, Uzbekistan with 8,131 tonnes against nil and Estonia with 8,050 tonnes compared to 703. Sugar imports in Oct/Mar 1995/96 were negligible (1,179 tonnes).

TENDERS - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) bought 13,000 tonnes of raw sugar for October delivery at $338.00 a tonne. GEZA cancelled the purchase of 13,000 tonnes of raws and 26,000 tonnes of white sugar which were contained in the same tender issued on August 29, trade sources said.
